subject: Clarify output & training carveouts — Brightline MSA/Order Form
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha@brightline.co>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@brightline.co
Date: 2025-04-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Brightline MSA/Order Form — IP questions and proposed redlines

Hi Sofia / Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team flagged a few areas in the attached MSA and Order Form where we need clarity before procurement can sign:

1) Output ownership: we expect to retain ownership of outputs generated from our data and prompts. Can you confirm Redwood will not claim ownership or use outputs for model training without explicit consent?
2) Training/data use: the current Order Form references a "feedback license" and broad "service improvements". We need an opt-in mechanism for training on sensitive data and a clear definition of what telemetry falls under the feedback license.
3) Auditability & retention: need confirmation of audit logs and a 90-day retention default for request logs (longer if we pay extra).

Attached: Brightline_MSADraft_v3.docx with our redlines in tracked changes.

Can you propose concrete redline language or one of your standard options that would be acceptable for both sides? Procurement would like a succinct path to sign (we have an internal deadline of 5/2).

Best,
Aisha Khan
Head of Product Ops, Brightline
A: +1 (415) 555-0124

[Attachment: Brightline_MSADraft_v3.docx (docx)]

From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: aisha@brightline.co
Date: 2025-04-22T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brightline MSA/Order Form — IP questions and proposed redlines

Team — forwarding Brightline's redlines and asks. High level: they want (a) output ownership retained by customer, (b) training opt-in for customer data, (c) audit/retention guarantees.

Context: we already offer a Customer Output carveout in our standard Order Form but Brightline has pushed back on the breadth of the "feedback license" in Section 7. Our product can implement an opt-in toggle for training on a per-API-key basis but the legal language needs to reflect operational constraints (telemetry retention, aggregated telemetry usage, and ability to remediate PI exposure).

Proposed approach for discussion (fast path to close):
- Option B (recommended): Customer retains output ownership; Redwood gets a narrow feedback license limited to aggregated/anonymous telemetry for service improvements and not for model training on Brightline prompts/content unless Brightline opts in via order form checkbox. Provide a 90-day default for request logs, with longer retention as an add-on.
- Option A (more permissive): Redwood retains right to use feedback for training but with stricter redaction obligations and option to opt-out on specified datasets — higher legal risk for them.
- Option C (customer-first): Customer retains output and all training rights; Redwood limited to product telemetry only (likely impact on pricing).

Action items:
1) Kimberly — can you draft precise redline text for Option B that maps to our product capabilities?
2) Karthik — confirm if ops can support a 90-day default + paid extension and what that SKU looks like.
3) Ben — propose a short external note to Aisha with the recommended path and next steps (DocuSign link preferred).

Sofia Ivanova
Director, Product — Platform
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, aisha@brightline.co
Date: 2025-04-22T14:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brightline MSA/Order Form — draft redline options

Sofia / team — attached is a short playbook and three redline options to present. TL;DR: Option B keeps us commercially viable while giving Brightline the opt-in protections they want.

Key redline language for Option B (to paste into their doc):
"Customer Output; Feedback License. Customer retains ownership of Outputs generated solely from Customer Content and prompts. Redwood may collect aggregated and non-identifiable usage metrics for service improvement. Redwood will not use Customer Content or Outputs to train or fine-tune models without the Customer’s explicit, written opt-in (e.g., checked box on the Order Form or signed addendum)."

Notes / risk:
- We should include a short carveout permitting (i) limited retention of request metadata for debugging and legal compliance, and (ii) automated anomaly detection that may use aggregated signals.
- We cannot commit to redacting every instance of PI prior to training unless Brightline pays for an additional sanitization offering.

Attachment: RDW_IP_Playbook_v2.docx (contains the redline snippets + recommended DocuSign addendum).

Please let me know if you want a tightened version for SOC/security review.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Legal
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: RDW_IP_Playbook_v2.docx (docx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha@brightline.co>
Cc: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-23T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Brightline MSA/Order Form — path to sign (recommended)

Hi Aisha — quick note with a proposed path to close that keeps your procurement timeline intact: 

1) We adopt Option B from our counsel (see excerpt below).
2) Redwood will add an Order Form checkbox for "Allow Redwood to use Customer Content/Outputs for model training" — unchecked by default.
3) Default retention for request logs: 90 days; we can provide 12-, 24-, or 36-month retention as a paid add-on.
4) We'll include audit/logging options in the addendum and a commitment to provide request-level logs for incident investigations under NDA.

Suggested one-line for the Order Form addendum (doc will be attached via DocuSign):
"Customer retains ownership of Outputs. Redwood may use aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry for service improvements. Redwood will not use Customer Content or Outputs to train models without explicit Customer opt-in as indicated on the Order Form."

If that sounds good, we'll send a DocuSign with the addendum + the MSA redlines for your counsel to confirm. Targeting a 48-hour turnaround if Brightline legal signs off.

DocuSign link (draft): https://docusign.com/r/BR-2025-0893-addendum (placeholder)

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-min call if you want to walk the language.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Ben / Aisha — thanks for the clear proposal. Brightline legal is comfortable with Option B subject to two small edits and one confirmation: 

1) Edit: Change "aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry" to "aggregated telemetry that cannot reasonably be used to reconstruct Customer Content or Outputs". Small wording tweak for clarity.
2) Edit: Add a definition for "opt-in" to reference the Order Form checkbox or a signed addendum.
3) Confirmation requested: Redwood to commit to providing request-level logs for security incidents within 10 business days under NDA; retention default 90 days (ok).
